zh: 由于有事，回到家只睡了一会儿，周少棠便已醒来，匆匆赶到杨家，杨书办正要出门。“你到哪里去？”“想到城隍山去看个朋友……”“不要去了。”同少棠不等他话完，便即打断，“我有要紧事同你商量。”“于是就在杨家密谈。周少棠将昨夜的经过情形，细细告诉了杨书办，问他的意见。“卖田他自己去卖好了，月如为啥说唐子韶不便出面？”“对！我当时倒忘记问她了。”“这且不言。”杨书办问道：“现在马大老爷那里应该怎么办？”“我正就是为这一点要来同你商量。月如打的是如意算盘，希望先报出去，顺利接收，那一来唐子韶一点责任都没有了。不过，要等他凑齐了银子再报，不怕耽误日子？如今我倒有个办法，”周少棠突然问道：“你有没有啥路子，能借一笔大款子？”“现在银根紧。”杨书办问：“你想借多少？”“不是我借。我想叫唐子韶先拿他的西湖田抵押一笔款子出来，我们先拿到了手，有多少算多少。”杨书办沉吟了好一会说：“这是出典。典田不如买田，这种主顾不多，而且，手续也很麻烦，不是三两无能办好的。”
en: With business on his mind, Zhou Shaotang woke after only a little sleep at home and hurried to Yang’s house. Clerk Yang was just going out. “Where are you off to?” “I thought I would visit a friend on City God Hill…” “Do not go.” Zhou interrupted him before he could finish. “I have something urgent to discuss with you.” They held their private conference at Yang’s house. Zhou gave a detailed account of the previous night and asked for his opinion. “Let him sell his own land. Why did Yueru say Tang Zishao could not appear in the transaction himself?” “Exactly! I forgot to ask her that.” “Leave that aside for now. What should we do about Magistrate Ma?” “That is precisely what I came to discuss. Yueru has it all nicely worked out: she hopes we shall first report that the takeover went smoothly. Then Tang will be free of all responsibility. But if we wait until he has raised the silver before submitting the report, will we not hold things up? I do have an idea, though.” Zhou suddenly asked, “Do you know anyone who could arrange a substantial loan?” “Money is tight at present. How much do you want to borrow?” “It is not for me. I want Tang to raise a loan against his West Lake fields. Let us get the money into our hands first, however much it is.” Yang thought for some time. “That means putting the land in pledge. Taking land in pledge is less attractive than buying it outright. There are not many people willing to do it, and the formalities are troublesome. It cannot be settled in two or three days.”

zh: 周少棠爽然若失，“照此看来，”他说：“一只煮熟的鸭子，只怕要飞掉了。”“这也不见得。如果相信得过，不妨先放他一马。”“就是因为相信不过。”周少棠说：“你想他肯拿小老婆来陪我……”周少棠自知泄漏了秘密，要想改口，已是驷不及舌。杨书办笑笑问道：“唷，你‘近水楼台先得是月’，同月如上过阳台了？”“没有，没有。”周少棠急忙分辩：“不过嘴巴亲一亲，胸脯摸一摸。总而言之，唐子韶一定在搞鬼，轻易相信他，一定会上当。““我晓得了。等我来想想。”公事上到底是杨书办比较熟悉，他认为有一个可进可退的办法，即是由马逢时先报一个公事，说是帐目上尚有疑义，正在查核之中，请准予暂缓结案。“唐子韶看到这样子一个活络说法，晓得一定逃不过门，会赶紧去想法子。如果他真的想赖掉，我们就把他的毛病和盘托出。虽没有好处，至少马大老爷也办了一趟漂亮差使。”“好极！就是这个办法。”周少棠说：“等下我们一起到公济典，索性同唐子韶明说：马大老爷已经定规了。事不宜迟，最好你现在就去通知马大老爷。”
en: Zhou looked crestfallen. “Then it seems our cooked duck may fly away after all.” “Not necessarily. If we can trust him, we might give him some leeway first.” “The trouble is that we cannot trust him. Think of it: he was willing to let his concubine entertain me…” Zhou realized he had let out a secret, but it was too late to call back his words. Yang smiled. “Well! The tower nearest the water catches the moon first. Have you been to bed with Yueru?” “No, no!” Zhou hastened to explain. “Only kissed her lips and felt her breasts. In any case, Tang must be up to something. We shall certainly be taken in if we trust him too readily.” “I see. Let me think.” Yang, after all, knew more about official procedure. He proposed a course that would leave them room to advance or retreat: Ma Fengshi should first submit a report stating that there were still doubtful points in the accounts, that they were being investigated, and that permission was requested to defer closing the case. “Once Tang sees a report that leaves the matter open, he will know he cannot get away and will hurry to find a solution. If he really tries to evade payment, we shall disclose every one of his irregularities. We may gain nothing ourselves, but at least Magistrate Ma will have carried out his commission creditably.” “Excellent! That is the way.” Zhou added, “When we go to Gongji Pawnshop together, let us tell Tang outright that Magistrate Ma has already decided. We should lose no time. You had better inform him now.”

zh: “他不在家，到梅花碑抚台衙门‘站班’去了。”原来巡抚定三、八为衙参之期，接着藩臬两司及任实缺、有差使的道员，候补的知县佐杂，都到巡抚衙门前面去“站班”，作为致敬的表示，目的是在博得好感，加深印象。这是小官候补的不二法门，有时巡抚与司道谈论公事，有个什么差使要派人，够资格保荐的司道，想起刚刚见过某人，正堪充任，因而获得意外机缘，亦是常有之事。“你同唐子韶约的是啥辰光？”“还早，还早。”周少棠说：“我们先到茶店里吃一壶茶再去。”“也不必到茶店里了。我有好六安茶，泡一壶你吃。”于是泡上六安茶，又端出两盘干点心，一面吃，一面谈闲天。杨书办问起月如，周少棠顿时眉飞色舞，不但毫不隐瞒，而且作了许多形容。
en: “He is not at home. He has gone to stand in attendance at the governor’s yamen at Meihuabei.” The governor held official audiences on days ending in three or eight. Following the provincial treasurer, the judicial commissioner and the circuit intendants holding substantive posts or special commissions, expectant county magistrates and subordinate officials would go to stand in attendance outside the governor’s yamen. This was a show of respect intended to win favour and strengthen the impression they made. For minor officials awaiting appointments, it was the surest road to advancement. Sometimes, while discussing business with the senior officials, the governor would need someone for a commission. A treasurer, commissioner or intendant entitled to recommend a candidate might remember a suitable man he had just seen. Such unexpected opportunities were by no means rare. “What time did you arrange to meet Tang?” “There is plenty of time yet,” Zhou said. “Let us have a pot of tea at a teashop first.” “No need to go out. I have some good Lu’an tea. I shall brew you a pot.” Yang made the tea and brought out two plates of dry pastries. They ate and chatted. When Yang asked about Yueru, Zhou grew animated at once. He concealed nothing and gave a wealth of description.

zh: 杨书办津津有味地听完，不由得问道：“如果有机会，月如肯不肯同你上床？”“我想一定会肯。其实昨天晚上，只要我胆子够大，也就上手了。”“你是怕唐子韶来捉你的奸，要你写‘伏辩’？”“不借。这是我们三个人的事，我不能做这种荒唐事，连累好朋友。”“少棠，你不做见色轻友的事，足见你够朋友。”杨书办说：“我倒问你，你到底想不想同月如困一觉？”“想是想，没有机会。”“我来给你弄个机会。”杨书办说：“等下，我到公济典去，绊住唐子韶的身子，你一个人闯到月如楼上，我保险不会有人来捉你们的奸。”“不必，不必！”周少棠心想，即令能这样顺利地真个消魂，也要顾虑到落一个话柄在杨书办手里。这种傻事决不能做，所以又加一句：“多谢盛情。不过我的胆还不够大，谢谢，谢谢。”杨书办倒是有心想助他成其好事，看他态度如此坚决，也就不便再说。只是付之一笑。
en: Yang listened with relish. “If you had the chance, would Yueru be willing to go to bed with you?” “I am sure she would. In fact, last night I could have had her if I had been bold enough.” “You were afraid Tang would catch you in the act and make you sign a confession?” “Exactly. This business concerns all three of us. I could not do anything so foolish and drag my friends into trouble.” “Shaotang, you would not put a pretty woman before your friends. That shows what a good friend you are. But tell me: do you want to sleep with Yueru or not?” “I do, but there is no opportunity.” “I shall make one for you. When we go to Gongji, I shall keep Tang occupied. You can go straight upstairs to Yueru. I guarantee that no one will catch you together.” “No need, no need!” Even if he could enjoy himself so easily, Zhou reflected, he would still have to consider the hold this would give Yang over him. He must never do anything so foolish. He therefore added, “Thank you for your kindness, but I am still not brave enough. Thank you, all the same.” Yang had genuinely meant to help him attain his desire. Seeing him so determined, however, he could hardly press the matter. He merely smiled.

zh: “不过，你倒提醒我了，我还是可以到月如那里去一趟，问问你提出来的那句话。”“这样说，仍旧我一个人到公济？”“不错，你先去，我问完了话，随后就来。”“那么，”杨书办问：“我在唐子韶面前，要不要说破？”“不必，你只说我随后就到便是。”近午时分，两人到了公济典旁边的那条巷子，暂且分手。周少棠来到唐家举手敲门，好久没有回音，只好快快回身，哪知一转身便发现月如冉冉而来，后面跟着她家的丫头，手里挽个菜篮，主婢俩是刚从小菜场回来。“碰得巧！”周少棠说：“如果你迟一步，或者我早来一步，就会不到面。”“周老爷，你也来得巧，今天难得买得新鲜菌子，你在我那里吃了中饭走。”“不，不！杨书办在公济等我。”“那就请杨书办一起来。”“等一息再说。阿嫂，我先到你这里坐一坐，我有句话想问你。”其实丫头已经去开了大门，进门就在客堂里坐。月如请他上楼，周少棠辞谢了，因为他不想多作逗留，只说两句话就要告辞，觉得不必累人家费事。
en: “You have reminded me of something, though. I could still call on Yueru and ask her that question you raised.” “Then I am to go to Gongji alone?” “Yes. You go ahead. I shall follow as soon as I have asked her.” “Should I tell Tang about it?” Yang asked. “No need. Just say I shall be along shortly.” Towards noon they reached the lane beside Gongji Pawnshop and parted for the moment. Zhou went to Tang’s house and knocked. After a long wait without an answer, he turned away in disappointment. As he did so, he saw Yueru approaching at an unhurried pace, her maid behind her with a market basket on her arm. Mistress and maid had just returned from buying food. “What good timing!” Zhou said. “A moment later for you, or a moment earlier for me, and we should have missed each other.” “You have come at just the right time too, Mr Zhou. I was lucky enough to find fresh mushrooms today. Stay for lunch.” “No, no! Clerk Yang is waiting for me at Gongji.” “Then invite him too.” “We shall see in a moment. Sister-in-Law, let me sit with you first. There is something I want to ask.” The maid had already opened the door. They went in and sat in the reception room. Yueru invited him upstairs, but he declined. He meant to stay only long enough for a few words and felt there was no need to put her to any trouble.

zh: “阿嫂，我想请问你，你昨天说卖西湖田，老唐不便出面。这是啥讲究？”不想问的是这句话，月如顿时一愣，同时也提醒她想起一件事，更加不安。看在周少棠眼里，颇有异样的感觉，尽头不由得疑云大起。“周老爷，你请坐一坐，我是突然之间想起有句话要先交代。”接着便喊：“阿翠，阿翠，你在做啥？客人来了也不泡茶。”“我在厨房里，烧开水。”阿翠高声答应着，走了出来。“你到桥边去关照一声，家里有客人，要他下半天再来。”阿翠发愣，一时想不起到“桥边”要关照什么人。“去啊！”“去，去，”阿翠嗫嚅着问：“去同哪个说？”“不是我们刚刚去过？叫他们老板马上来？”“喔，喔！”阿翠想起来了，“木器店、木器店。”说着，转身而去。“真笨！”月如咕哝着，转身说道，“对不起，对不起！周老爷，你刚才要问我的那句话，我没有听清楚。”
en: “Sister-in-Law, yesterday you said Old Tang could not appear in person to sell the West Lake fields. Why is that?” Yueru had not expected this question. She was taken aback, and it also reminded her of something else, making her still more uneasy. Zhou sensed something strange in her reaction, and suspicions began to cloud his mind. “Please sit for a moment, Mr Zhou. I have suddenly remembered an instruction I must give first.” She called, “A’cui! A’cui! What are you doing? We have a guest, and you have not even made tea.” “I am in the kitchen boiling water,” A’cui answered loudly, coming out. “Go to the bridge and tell him we have a guest. Ask him to come this afternoon instead.” A’cui stared blankly. For the moment she could not think whom she was to inform at the bridge. “Go on!” “Yes, yes,” she faltered. “Whom am I to tell?” “Did we not just go there and ask the owner to come at once?” “Oh, yes! The furniture shop, the furniture shop.” She turned and left. “What a fool!” Yueru muttered. Turning back, she said, “Forgive me, Mr Zhou. I did not quite catch your question.”

zh: “老唐卖田，为啥不便出面。”月如原来是因为唐子韶突然要卖田，风声传出去，惹人猜疑，莫非他要离开杭州了，是不是回安徽老家？这一来会影响他们开溜的计划，所以不便出面。如今的回答，当然改过了。“公济典一查封，我们老爷有亏空，大概总有人晓得，不晓得也会问，为啥卖田。如果晓得卖田是为亏空，就一定会杀价，所以他是不出面的好。”理由很充分，语气亦从容，周少棠疑虑尽释，“到底阿嫂细心。”他站起身来：“我就是这句话，问清楚了要走了。”出了唐家往公济典，走不多远，迎面遇见阿翠，甩着一条长辫子，一扭一扭地走了过来，“周老爷，”她开口招呼：“要回去了。”“不，我到公济典去。”“喏，”阿翠回身一指，“这里一直过去，过一座小桥，就是公济典后门。”周少棠本来要先出巷子上了大街从公济典前门入内，现在既有捷径可通后门，落得省点气力，“谢谢你。”他含笑致谢：“原来还有后门。”“走后门要省好多路。”阿翠又加一句客气话：“周老爷有空常常来。”
en: “Why can Old Tang not show himself when selling the land?” Yueru’s real reason was that a sudden sale by Tang would start rumours and suspicions. Was he leaving Hangzhou? Was he returning to his old home in Anhui? Such talk would interfere with their plans to slip away, which was why he could not appear himself. Naturally, she now gave a different answer. “Since Gongji has been taken into official custody, some people probably know that our master has a shortfall in his accounts. Even those who do not will ask why he is selling land. Once they learn that he needs the money to make good a deficit, they are bound to force down the price. It is better for him to keep out of sight.” The reason was persuasive, and her tone composed. Zhou’s suspicions vanished. “You really do think of everything, Sister-in-Law.” He stood up. “That was all I wanted to ask. Now I understand, I must go.” He had not gone far towards Gongji when he met A’cui coming back, her long plait swinging as she walked with a sway. “Going home, Mr Zhou?” she greeted him. “No, I am going to Gongji.” “Look.” She turned and pointed. “Straight along here, over a little bridge, and you are at Gongji’s back entrance.” Zhou had intended to leave the lane, reach the main street and enter by the front. A shortcut to the rear would save him some effort. “Thank you,” he said with a smile. “So there is a back entrance too.” “It saves a good deal of walking.” She added politely, “Do come and see us often, Mr Zhou, whenever you have time.”

zh: 见她如此殷勤，周少棠想起一件事，昨夜在唐家作客，照便应该开发赏钱，因而唤住她说：“ 阿翠你等等。”说着，探手入怀，皮袍子口袋中，有好几块碎银子，摸了适中的一块，约莫三四钱重，递向阿翠。“周老爷，这作啥？”“这个给你。昨天我走的时候忘记掉了。”“不要，不要。”“不许说不要。”周少棠故意板一板脸：“没规矩。”于是阿翠笑着道了谢，高高兴兴地甩着辫子回去。周少棠便照她的指点，一直往前走，果然看到一座小石桥，桥边一家旧货店，旧木器都堆到路上来了。周少棠心中一动，站住脚细看了一会，并没有发现什么木器店。不由得奇怪，莫非月如所说的木器店，即是指这家旧货店？这样想着，便上前问讯：“老板，请问这里有家木器店在哪里？”“不晓得。”旧货店老板诧异，“从没有听说过这里有家木器店。哪个跟你说的？骗你来‘撞木钟’。”“是……”周少棠疑云大起，决意弄个水落石出，“只怕我听错了，公济典唐朝奉家说这里有家木器店，要同你买木器。”“你不是听错了，就是弄错了。不是买木器，是要卖木器，叫我去看货估价。““她为啥要……”周少棠突然将话顿住了，闲事已经管得太多了，再问下去，会惹人猜疑，因而笑一笑，说一声：“是我弄错了。”扬长而去。
en: Her attentiveness reminded Zhou of something. As a guest at Tang’s house the previous night, he should have given the servants a tip. “A’cui, wait a moment,” he called. Reaching inside his fur-lined robe, he felt among several pieces of silver in a pocket and chose one of a suitable size, weighing perhaps three or four tenths of a tael. He held it out. “What is this for, Mr Zhou?” “For you. I forgot when I left yesterday.” “No, no!” “You must not refuse.” He put on a stern face. “That would be bad manners.” A’cui smiled, thanked him and went happily on her way, swinging her plait. Zhou followed her directions. Sure enough, he came to a little stone bridge. Beside it stood a second-hand shop, with old wooden furniture piled out into the roadway. Something struck him. He stopped and looked carefully around but could see no furniture shop. Could Yueru have meant this second-hand dealer? He went over to ask. “Excuse me, where is the furniture shop around here?” “I have no idea,” the dealer answered in surprise. “I have never heard of one. Who told you that? Someone is sending you on a fool’s errand.” “It was…” Suspicion rose again, and Zhou resolved to get to the bottom of it. “Perhaps I heard wrongly. At Master Tang’s house—the pawnbroker from Gongji—they said there was a furniture shop here and they wanted to buy some furniture from you.” “Either you heard wrongly or you have got it wrong. They want to sell furniture, not buy it. They asked me to look it over and give them a price.” “Why does she want to…” Zhou broke off. He had meddled quite enough already. More questions would arouse suspicion. He smiled, said, “My mistake,” and strode away.

zh: 到了公济典，只见唐子韶的神气很难看，是懊恼与忧虑交杂的神情。可想而知，杨书办已将他们所决定的处置告诉他了。不过，看到周少棠，他仍旧摆出一副尊敬而亲热的神情，迎上前来，握着周少棠的手说，“老大哥，你无论如何要帮我一个忙。”“啥事情？”周少棠装做不知，一面问，一面坐了下来，顺便跟杨书办交换了一个眼色，相戒谨慎。“老杨告诉我，马大老爷预备报公事，说我帐目不清。”唐子韶的话说得很急：“公事上怎么好这样说？”“这也无所谓，你把帐目弄清楚，不就没事了吗？”“话不是这样说，好比落了一个脚印在那里。有这件案底在衙门里，我以后做人做事就难了。”“那么，你想怎么样呢？”“咦！”唐子韶手指着说：“周先生，你不是答应我的，请马大老爷暂时把公事压一压？”“压也不过是一天半天的事。”杨书办插了一句嘴。“一两天哪里来得及？”唐子韶说：“现在银根又紧。”“好了，我晓得了。”周少棠说：“老唐，外头做事，一定要上路，不上路，人家要帮忙也无从帮起。这样子，你尽快去想办法，我同老杨替你到马大老爷那里讨个情，今天晚上再同你碰头。”说完，他已经站了起来，准备离去。“
en: At Gongji he found Tang looking very unhappy, with an expression compounded of vexation and anxiety. Clearly Yang had told him what they had decided to do. Nevertheless, Tang greeted Zhou with a show of warmth and respect, coming forward to clasp his hand. “My dear elder brother, you must help me, whatever happens.” “What is it?” Zhou asked, pretending ignorance as he sat down. He exchanged a glance with Yang, warning him to be cautious. “Old Yang tells me Magistrate Ma intends to submit a report saying my accounts are not clear.” Tang spoke urgently. “How can he put that in an official report?” “What does it matter? Put the accounts in order, and that will be the end of it.” “That is not how it works. It is like leaving a footprint. With such a record against me at the yamen, it will be difficult for me to do anything or hold up my head afterwards.” “Then what do you want?” “Why, Mr Zhou!” Tang pointed at him. “Did you not promise to ask Magistrate Ma to hold the matter back for a while?” “Only for a day or half a day,” Yang put in. “What can I do in a day or two? Money is so tight now.” “All right, I understand,” Zhou said. “Old Tang, a man doing business must know how to behave. If you do not, others cannot help you even if they wish to. Let us do this: find a way as quickly as you can, while Old Yang and I plead with Magistrate Ma for you. We shall meet again this evening.” He had already risen to leave.

zh: “不忙，不忙！”唐子韶急忙说道：“我已经叫人去叫菜了，吃了饭再走。”“饭不吃了。”周少棠灵机一动，故意吓他一吓，“说实话，我们到你这里来，已经有人在钉梢了，还是早点走的好。”这一下，不但唐子韶吃惊，也吓了杨书办，脸上变色，悄悄问道：“是哪里的人？在哪里？”“杭州府的人，你出去就看到了。”说着，往外就走，杨书办紧紧跟在后面。“两位慢慢！”唐子韶追上来问：“晚上怎么样碰头？”“我会来看你。”“好，恭候大驾。”于是周少棠领头扬长而去，出了公济典，不断回头看，杨书办神色紧张地问：“人在哪里？”周少棠“噗哧”一声笑了出来，“对不起，对不起，害得你都受惊了。”他说：“我们到城隍山去吃油蓑饼，我详详细细告诉你。”
en: “No hurry, no hurry!” Tang said hastily. “I have sent someone to order dishes. Have lunch before you go.” “We shall not stay for lunch.” A sudden idea occurred to Zhou, and he deliberately gave Tang a fright. “To tell the truth, someone has been watching us since we came here. We had better leave at once.” This alarmed not only Tang but Yang, whose face changed colour. “Whose men?” he asked quietly. “Where are they?” “Men from the Hangzhou prefecture. You will see when you go out.” Zhou started for the door, with Yang close behind. “Wait a moment, both of you!” Tang hurried after them. “How shall we meet this evening?” “I shall come to see you.” “Very well. I shall await your visit.” Zhou strode out in front. Once outside Gongji, he kept looking back. Yang asked anxiously, “Where are they?” Zhou burst out laughing. “Forgive me! I have even frightened you. Let us go up City God Hill for yousuobing cakes. I shall tell you everything.”

zh: 上了城隍山，在药师间壁的酒店落座，老板姓陈，是周少棠的熟人，也认识杨书办，亲自从帐桌上起身来招待。“这么冷的天气，两位倒有兴致上城隍山？难得、难得。”陈老板问：“要吃点啥？”“特为来吃油蓑饼。”周少棠说：“菜随便，酒要好。”“有一坛好花雕，卖得差不多了，还剩下来三斤，够不够？”“中午少吃点，够了。”“我上回吃过的‘一鸡四吃’，味道不错，”杨书办说：“照样再来一回。鸡要肥。”“杨先生放心好了。”于是烫上酒来，先用现成的小菜、发芽豆、茶油鱼干这类下酒。这时周少棠告诉杨书办，根本没有人钉梢，只是故意吓一吓唐子韶而已。
en: They climbed City God Hill and sat down in the tavern next to Yaoshi. Its owner, surnamed Chen, knew Zhou well and also knew Yang. He rose from his account desk to attend to them himself. “What brings you up City God Hill in such cold weather? A rare pleasure! What would you like?” “We came especially for yousuobing. Any dishes will do, but the wine must be good,” Zhou said. “I have a jar of fine Huadiao, almost all sold. Three jin remain. Will that be enough?” “We shall drink less at noon. That will do.” “Last time I had your ‘one chicken, four ways,’ and it was excellent,” Yang said. “Let us have it again. Make sure the chicken is fat.” “Leave it to me, Mr Yang.” The wine was heated, and they began with ready-made small dishes: sprouted beans, dried fish in tea-seed oil and the like. Zhou now told Yang that nobody had been watching them. He had merely meant to frighten Tang.

zh: “不过，有件事很奇怪，月如不晓得在搞啥花样。”等周少棠细说了他发现唐家要卖木器的经过，杨书办立刻下了一个判断：“唐子韶要带了他的小老婆，逃之夭夭了。”周少棠也是如此看法，“逃到哪里呢？”他问：“不会逃到徽州吧？”“逃回徽州，还是可以抓回来的。只有逃到上海，在租界里躲了起来，只要他自己小心，不容易抓到。”杨书办又说：“我看他用的缓兵之计，卖田最快也要十天半个月，要开溜，时间上足足够用。”“嗯，嗯。那么，我们应该怎么办呢？”杨书办亦无善策，默默地喝了一会酒，突然之间，将酒杯放下，双手靠在桌上，身上前倾，低声说道：“我同你说实话，你刚刚开玩笑，说有人‘钉梢’，我当时心里心上八下，难过极了。俗语说得，‘日里不做亏心事，夜半敲门心不惊’。发横财也要命的，强求不来。这件事，我们作成马大老爷立一场功劳，关照他据实呈报；唐子韶自作自受，不必可惜。你看如何？”周少棠想了一下，点点头：“我同意。不过数目要打个折扣。”“为啥？”“咦！我不是同你讲过，胡大先生要报月如的情，我们原来预备分给他一份，他不要，算是送月如。所以唐子韶作弊的数目不能实报。”
en: “There is something very strange, though. I cannot make out what Yueru is up to.” Once Zhou had described his discovery that the Tangs meant to sell their furniture, Yang reached an immediate conclusion. “Tang is going to take his concubine and run away.” Zhou thought so too. “Where would he go? Surely not back to Huizhou?” “If he fled to Huizhou, they could still bring him back. His only chance is Shanghai. If he hides in the foreign settlements and takes care, he will not be easy to catch. I think he is playing for time. Selling land takes ten days or half a month at the very least. That would give him more than enough time to slip away.” “Yes, yes. Then what should we do?” Yang had no good answer either. They drank in silence for a while. Suddenly he set down his cup, rested both hands on the table and leaned forward. In a low voice he said, “I shall be honest with you. When you joked just now about someone watching us, I was in a terrible state. As the saying goes, do nothing shameful by day and you need not fear a knock at midnight. A windfall can cost a man his life. You cannot force it. Let us give Magistrate Ma a chance to earn some credit. Tell him to report the facts. Tang has brought this on himself; we need not pity him. What do you say?” Zhou considered, then nodded. “I agree. But the amount must be reduced.” “Why?” “Did I not tell you? Mr Hu wants to repay Yueru’s kindness. We had meant to give him a share, but he does not want it. He is making it a present to Yueru. So we cannot report the full amount Tang has embezzled.”

zh: 这段话中的“胡大先生”四字，不知怎么让陈老板听到了，便踱过来打听他的消息，少不得嗟叹惋惜一番。周少棠他们的座位临窗，窗子是碎锦格子糊上白纸，中间嵌一方玻璃，望出去一株华盖亭亭的不凋松，春秋佳日，树下便是极好的茶座，陈老板指着说道：“那株松树下面，就是胡大先生同王抚台第一次来吃茶、吃酒的地方。王抚台有一回来过，还特为提起，这句话十七八年了。”“王抚台如果晓得胡大先生会有今天这种下场，只怕他死不瞑目。”杨书办感慨不止，“这样子轰轰烈烈的事业，说败就败，真同年大将军一样。”“比年大将军总要好得多。”周少棠说：“至少，性命之忧是不会有的。”陈老板接口说道：“就算没有性命之忧，活得也没意思了。”“是啊！”杨书办深深点头：“爬得高，跌得重，还是看开点好。”
en: Somehow the words “Mr Hu” reached Chen’s ears. He strolled over to ask for news, and naturally there were sighs and expressions of regret. Zhou and Yang sat beside a window of intricate latticework covered in white paper, with a square of glass set into the middle. Through it they could see an evergreen pine, its lofty crown spreading like a canopy. On fine days in spring and autumn, the space beneath it made an excellent place for tea. Chen pointed. “Under that pine is where Mr Hu and Governor Wang sat the first time they came for tea and wine. Governor Wang mentioned it particularly on a later visit. That was seventeen or eighteen years ago.” “If Governor Wang knew how Mr Hu would end, I doubt he could rest in his grave,” Yang said with deep feeling. “Such a magnificent enterprise, gone just like that! Exactly like General Nian.” “Still, he is much better off than General Nian,” Zhou said. “At least his life is not in danger.” “Even if his life is safe,” Chen added, “what pleasure can there be left in living?” “True.” Yang nodded gravely. “The higher you climb, the harder you fall. Better to take things less to heart.”

zh: 就这样一直在谈胡雪岩，直到酒醉饭饱，相偕下山，周少棠方又提到唐子韶，“我答应过他，只算两万四千银子。”他说：“你同马大老爷去说，要报就报这个数目好了。”“好的。”杨书办说：“不过，你应该同胡大先生去说说清楚，现在是照他的意思，看在唐子韶小老婆分上，特为少报。我们三个人是随公事。不然，他只以为我们从中弄了多少好处，岂不冤枉。”他又加了一句：“这句话请你一定要说到。”由于杨书办的态度很认真，周少棠决走到元宝街去一趟。胡雪岩已经不会客了，但对周少棠的情分不同，仍旧将他请了进去，动问来意。“你说的那匹‘瘦马’我见过了，亦就是见一见，没有别的花样。”周少棠说：“他亏空至少有八万银子，照你的意思，打了他一个三折，公事一报上去，当然要追。追出来抵还你的官款，也不无小补。”
en: They went on talking about Hu until they had eaten and drunk their fill. Only as they walked down the hill together did Zhou return to Tang. “I promised him we would count only twenty-four thousand taels. Tell Magistrate Ma that if he submits a report, that is the figure he should use.” “Very well,” Yang said. “But you ought to explain it all to Mr Hu. We are reducing the amount out of consideration for Tang’s concubine, just as he wished. The three of us are simply following official procedure. Otherwise he may think we have made a fortune out of it. That would be unfair to us.” He added, “Please be sure to tell him that.” Yang spoke so earnestly that Zhou decided to visit Yuanbao Street. Hu was no longer receiving visitors, but his affection for Zhou was different. He had him shown in and asked what had brought him. “I have seen that ‘slender horse’ you spoke of. Only seen her—nothing more,” Zhou said. “Tang’s deficit comes to at least eighty thousand taels. In accordance with your wishes, we have cut it to thirty per cent. Once the report goes in, they will of course have to recover it. Whatever they collect can go towards repaying the government money you owe. It will be of some help.”

zh: 一听这话，胡雪岩的眼圈发红，“少棠，”他说：“有你这句话就够了。从出事到现在，再好的朋友，都是同我来算帐的，顶多说是打个折扣，少还一点，没有人说一句，我介绍来的那笔存款，不要紧，摆在那里再说，帮我去弄钱来的，可以说没有。其中只有两个人，一个是古应春，帮我凑了二三十万银子，应付上海的风潮；再一个是你。古应春受过我的好处，大家原是有往来的，象你，该当凭你本事弄来的外款不要，移过来替我补亏空，虽说杯水车薪，无济于事，不过，我看来这两万四千银子，比什么都贵重。““大先生，你不要这样说。从前我也受过你的好处。”周少棠又说：“今天中午，我们在城隍山吃油蓑饼，还提起你同王抚台的交情，只怕他听得你有这一场风波，在阴司里都不安心。”提到玉有龄，枨触前尘，怀念故友，胡雪岩越发心里酸酸地想哭，“真正是一场大梦！”他说：“梦终归是梦，到底是要醒的。”“一个人能够象你做这样一场梦，古往今来，只怕也不过数得出来的几个人。”
en: Hu’s eyes reddened. “Shaotang, those words alone are enough. Since my troubles began, even my closest friends have come to settle accounts with me. At most they offer to knock something off and let me repay a little less. Not one has said, ‘Never mind that deposit I brought you. Leave it there for now.’ As for helping me raise money, you could say there has been nobody. Only two exceptions: Gu Yingchun, who helped scrape together two or three hundred thousand taels to meet the panic in Shanghai, and you. Gu has benefited from me; we have always helped one another. But you are giving up money you could rightfully earn by your own abilities and diverting it to make good my deficit. A cup of water on a cartload of burning wood, perhaps—too little to save anything. Yet to me these twenty-four thousand taels are more precious than anything else.” “Mr Hu, you must not put it that way. I too benefited from you in the old days.” Zhou went on, “At noon today we were having yousuobing on City God Hill and spoke of your friendship with Governor Wang. If he heard of this disaster, I doubt he could be at peace even in the other world.” The mention of Wang Youling brought back the past and his lost friend. Hu felt still more painfully close to tears. “It has all been one great dream,” he said. “A dream is a dream. In the end one has to wake.” “From ancient times to the present, there can have been only a handful of men who ever dreamed a dream like yours.”

zh: 这话使得胡雪岩颇受鼓舞，忽然想到他从未想过的身后之名，“不晓得将来说书的人，会不会说我？”他问：“说我又是怎样子地说，是骂我自作孽，还是运气不好？”“说是一定会说的，好比年大将军一样，哪个不晓得？”这使得胡雪岩想起年大将军赠妾的故事，心中一动，便笑一笑说：“我哪里比得上年大将军？不讲这些了。老弟兄聊聊家常。少棠，你今年贵庚？”“我属老虎，今年五十四。”“嫂夫人呢？”“她属羊，”比我小五岁。“周少棠说：”照道理，羊落虎口，我应该克她，哪晓得她的身子比我还健旺。““你也一点都不象五十几岁的人。”胡雪岩说：“嫂夫人我还是年纪轻的时候见过。那时候，我看你就有点怕她。现在呢？”“都一把年纪了，谈啥哪个怕哪个？而况……”“怎么不说下去？”胡雪岩问。这是因为说到周少棠伤心之处了，不愿多谈，摇摇头说：“没有啥。”
en: These words encouraged Hu. Suddenly he thought of something that had never occurred to him before: his reputation after death. “I wonder whether storytellers will tell of me one day. And if they do, what will they say? That I brought ruin upon myself, or that my luck failed?” “They certainly will tell your story. Just like General Nian—who has not heard of him?” This reminded Hu of the story of General Nian giving away a concubine. An idea stirred in him. He smiled. “How could I compare with General Nian? Let us leave that aside and talk of family matters, as old friends should. Shaotang, how old are you this year?” “I was born in the Year of the Tiger. Fifty-four.” “And your wife?” “The Year of the Sheep, five years younger. In theory, with a sheep in a tiger’s jaws, my influence ought to harm her. Yet her health is even better than mine.” “You do not look in your fifties at all. I last saw your wife when we were young. I thought you were a little afraid of her then. What about now?” “At our age, what does it matter who fears whom? Besides…” “Why stop there?” Hu asked. Zhou had reached a painful subject and did not wish to speak of it. He shook his head. “It is nothing.”

zh: “一定有缘故。少棠，你有啥苦衷，何妨同我讲一讲。”“不是有啥苦衷。”周少棠说：“我们的独养儿子……”周少棠的独子，这年正好三十，在上海一家洋行中做事，颇得“大板”‘的器重，当此海禁大开，洋务发达之时，可说前程如锦。哪知这年二月间，一场春瘟，竟尔不治。周太太哭得死去活来。周少棠本来要说的一句话是：“而况少年夫妻老来伴，独养儿子死掉了，我同她真正叫相依为命。”原来是提到了这段伤心之事，所以说不下去。胡雪岩便问：“你儿子娶亲了没有呢？”“没有。”“怎么三十岁还不成家？”“那是因为他学洋派，说洋人都是这样的，三十岁才成家。他又想跟他们老板到外国去学点本事，成了家不方便，所以耽误下来的。如今是连孙子都耽误了。“
en: “There must be a reason. Shaotang, if something is troubling you, why not tell me?” “It is not that. Our only son…” Zhou’s only son had been thirty that year. He worked for a foreign firm in Shanghai and was highly valued by its chief. With maritime restrictions lifted and foreign business flourishing, his prospects had seemed splendid. Then, in the second month, a spring epidemic had carried him off. Mrs Zhou had been beside herself with grief. What Zhou had begun to say was, “Besides, a young husband and wife become companions in old age. With our only son dead, she and I truly have no one but each other.” It was this painful memory that had stopped him. “Had your son married?” Hu asked. “No.” “Why was he still unmarried at thirty?” “He had taken to foreign ways. He said foreigners did not marry until thirty. He also wanted to go abroad with his employer and learn something useful. Marriage would have made that inconvenient, so he kept putting it off. Now that delay has cost us even a grandson.”

zh: “是啊！不孝有三，无后为大。”胡雪岩说：“嫂夫人倒没有劝你讨个小？”“提过。我同她说……”周少棠突然顿住，因为他原来的话是：“算了，算了，‘若要家不和，讨个小老婆’。”话到嘴边，想起忌讳：第一，螺蛳太太就是“小老婆”；第二，胡雪岩家“十二金钗”，“小老婆”太多，或许就是落到今天这个下场的原因。总之，令人刺心的话，决不可说。于是他改口说道：“内人虽有这番好意，无奈一时没有合便宜的人，只好敬谢不敏了。”“这倒是实话，要有合适的人，是顶要紧的一桩。‘若要家不合，讨个小老婆’，大家总以为指大太太吃醋，其实不然！讨小讨得不好，看大太太老实好欺侮，自己恃宠而骄，要爬到大太太头上。那一来大太太再贤惠，还是要吵架。”周少棠没有想到自己认为触犯忌讳的那句俗语，倒是胡雪岩自己说了出来。不过他的话也很有道理，螺蛳太太固然是个现成的例子；古应春纳妾的经过，他也知道。都可以为他的话作注脚。
en: “Yes. Of the three offences against filial duty, leaving no heir is the worst,” Hu said. “Has your wife not urged you to take a concubine?” “She has. I told her…” Zhou stopped abruptly. What he had actually said was, “Forget it. If you want discord at home, take a concubine.” As the words reached his lips, he remembered how offensive they might be. First, Madam Luosi was herself a concubine. Second, Hu’s household had its “Twelve Beauties.” Perhaps having so many concubines was part of what had brought him to his present plight. In any event, words that would wound him must not be spoken. Zhou changed his answer. “My wife meant it kindly, but I could not find a suitable woman just then. I could only decline with thanks.” “That is true enough. Finding the right woman is the most important thing. ‘If you want discord at home, take a concubine.’ People always assume this means the principal wife grows jealous. It need not be so at all! Choose badly, and the concubine sees a quiet principal wife whom she can bully. Spoiled by her husband’s favour, she tries to climb over the wife’s head. Then there will be quarrels, however virtuous the wife may be.” Zhou had not expected Hu himself to quote the very saying he had thought too delicate to mention. Yet there was much truth in his words. Madam Luosi was a ready example; Zhou also knew what had happened when Gu Yingchun took a concubine. Both experiences could serve as footnotes to Hu’s argument.
